tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (asking which images will be deleted, whether safe to apply a policy, why an image disappeared), lists explicit trigger contexts including ECS/Batch/Lambda/App Runner scenarios, and explicitly excludes out-of-scope contexts. It is concise, staying within a short paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks which images a lifecycle policy will delete or expire, whether it is safe to apply or keep a lifecycle policy, whether an image used by ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner or direct pulls is at risk, why an image disappeared from ECR, or to review lifecycle policies across repositories.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into project-specific conventions (verdict tiers, check matrix, scope resolution rules) without explaining general concepts like what ECR or lifecycle policies are. All content is domain-specific and non-obvious.
tests.evidence: "Tier (a): `lastRecordedPullTime` present. Authoritative. ECR refreshes it at least once every 24 hours, so a pull in the last day may not show yet; absence is never proof of non use."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (API call shapes, error tables, full simulation procedures, permission tables) is consistently delegated to references/ files via conditional loads at specific steps, rather than embedded inline.
tests.evidence: "Call shapes, fields, pagination, errors and known quirks are in [ecr-api-reference.md](references/ecr-api-reference.md), loaded at Step 1."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies when to load it (e.g., at Step 1, on AccessDenied, when a verdict is contested, at Step 9).
tests.evidence: "[permissions.md](references/permissions.md): IAM action table, preview approval wording, evaluation tool flag. Load on `AccessDenied`."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with the references/ prefix, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (verdict assignment, push correlation rule, preview-then-fallback sequencing) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible areas like how to present a brief decline are given short flexible wording ('decline in one sentence').
tests.evidence: "Tier (c) yields `Expiring-InUse` only when a qualifying pull remains more than 60 seconds after push."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where a choice exists (preview vs simulation), a clear default is designated with fallback only when the default cannot complete.
tests.evidence: "Preview is the source of truth. Try `StartLifecyclePolicyPreview` on every run. Only when it cannot complete, simulate, labelling every simulated number `SIMULATED`."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (resolve scope, read policy/images, preview, cross-reference, assign verdicts, render report) applicable to any repository/account, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Step 1. Resolve scope. Account, Region(s), repositories, draft policy if any, pull window."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes numerous concrete gotchas embedded throughout, such as the push correlation rule and ECR's 24-hour pull time refresh lag, which are non-obvious environment-specific facts.
tests.evidence: "ECR refreshes it at least once every 24 hours, so a pull in the last day may not show yet; absence is never proof of non use."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides an output template via report-template.md, satisfying the need for structured report output.
tests.evidence: "The only acceptable output is the report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large template is embedded inline in the body; the report structure is referenced from report-template.md rather than reproduced in full.
tests.evidence: "Render from [report-template.md](references/report-template.md) with its `##` headings in order, Scope through Next Steps"
